# First-party PostScript fixtures

`generate.py` authors all CFF1/CFF2 curves, subroutines, glyph aliases, CID font
DICTIONARIES, matrices and variation masters in this folder. It uses FontTools
as build tooling. The hybrid TTF reuses the existing first-party variation fixture.
All authored assets are GPL-3.0-only; no installed or proprietary font bytes are
included. `provenance.json` records byte counts and SHA-256 values.

The variable master has width 60/100/180 at weight 100/400/900 and an authored avar
mapping 650 to effective normalized 13107/16384. Independent test expectations
come from the analytic cumulative cubic control points, not another invocation
of the Rust renderer. Tiny contours use `T2CharString.setProgram`, which clears
previous compiled bytecode; assigning `.program` alone does not regenerate it.
The generator uses exact raw BCD for decimal matrix boundary cases rather than
FontTools' ordinary eight-significant-digit encoding.

`invalid-*`, `ambiguous-*` and command-limit assets are deliberate refusal cases.
The normal-consumer fonts add cmap aliases to the same analytic outlines; they
are never substituted for system font data in the native catalogue evidence.

Regenerate explicitly with:

```sh
python3 crates/ravet-surface/tests/fixtures/postscript/generate.py
```

This is acceptance tooling, not a runtime font-discovery or installation API.

All 31 authored OTF/TTF sources were regenerated byte-for-byte with the recorded
FontTools tooling before qualification. Metadata byte-boundary admission and
duplicate-role refusal remain separate checks; the byte limit does not override
operator, operand, FD or source-coordinate policies.
